citation: Louis Kurz, 'Chicago Water Works', tinted lithograph, Chicago Lithographing Co. for Jevne & Almini, in Chicago Illustrated (Chicago: Jevne & Almini, 1866-67). Chicago History Museum, ICHi-06859.
author: Louis Kurz, artist; Chicago Lithographing Co., printer; Jevne & Almini, publishers
describes_date: 1866-67 (the works as designed and building; the tower was finished in 1869)
repository: Chicago History Museum, ICHi-06859, shown on The Great Chicago Fire and the Web of Memory's Water Tower page. Not committed to this repository.
locator: The whole plate: the view north-east across Chicago Avenue to the tower, the pumping works behind it across Pine Street, and the lake beyond. The tower stands alone on open ground: a lawn with low shrub beds before it, raised plank walks and kerbs along Chicago Avenue and Pine Street leading to it, a row of young trees on the open ground to its west, and no house between the tower and Chicago Avenue. A house with a verandah stands at the plate's left edge, behind an iron fence.
rights_note: A lithograph published in Chicago in 1866-67; the Museum's copy is a faithful reproduction of a public-domain print. Read for layout only; nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-21 (T-3689) from the Web of Memory's 920-pixel copy of ICHi-06859.
note: Drawn while the works were building, so it shows the intended setting; the tower's grounds read the same in the 1890 photograph (chm_ichi_05902_water_tower_1890).
what_it_supplies: that the tower stood on open, planted ground with no houses between it and Chicago Avenue
walks and kerbs along Chicago Avenue and Pine Street before the tower
